sections.h2: Where is Hoffman Estates, Illinois, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Hoffman Estates is a village in the northwest suburbs, mostly in Cook County with a very small part in Kane County. It covers 21.07 square miles of land and uses ZIP codes 60169, 60010 and 60192.

German settlers had farmed the area west of Roselle Road and north of Golf Road, then called Wildcat Grove. In 1954 Sam and Jack Hoffman, a father and son who ran a construction company, bought 160 acres and began building homes. Residents voted to incorporate, and the village was incorporated on September 23, 1959. Annexations north of the Northwest Tollway in the early 1960s more than doubled its land area.

The village had 22,238 people in 1970 and 52,530 in the 2020 census. The count rose from 8,296 in 1960 to 46,363 in 1990, so many houses are several decades old, and a buyer will ask how old the roof, furnace and windows are.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Hoffman Estates homeowners?
sections.html:
QuickFacts gives a July 1, 2025 estimate of 50,858 residents, a 3.2 percent drop from the April 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it shows a 74.2 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $351,900, and 18,537 households averaging 2.75 people. Median gross rent is $1,734 and the median household income is $106,806.

Two other figures stand out. About 35.4 percent of residents were born outside the United States, and 46.4 percent of residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home. About 90.5 percent had not moved in the past year.

  • About 25.8 percent of homes are not owner-occupied, so tenant-occupied houses and small investor sales are part of the local market.
  • A multilingual community means a seller may want listing documents and showing instructions in more than one language.
  • The 2020 census listed 19,160 housing units, 3.5 percent of them vacant.

sections.h2: What jobs and businesses drive the local economy?
sections.html:
The Prairie Stone Business Park, a 750-acre planned district bounded by Illinois Route 59, Interstate 90, Illinois Route 72 and Beverly Road, anchors the village's employment. It took shape after Sears relocated its headquarters there in 1993, and it later added the 11,000-seat NOW Arena, a Marriott hotel and the Poplar Creek Crossing retail center.

The Wikipedia list of largest employers for 2023 puts St. Alexius Medical Center first at 2,500 workers, followed by Siemens Medical Systems and Claire's at 400 each, the Village of Hoffman Estates at 370, and FANUC America and Vistex at 350 each. Many Japanese companies also base their U.S. headquarters in Hoffman Estates and neighboring Schaumburg.

Corporate relocations and job changes are a common reason a household needs to sell on a short clock. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute at 28.5 minutes, and Woodfield Mall in Schaumburg, which opened in 1971, made the area a regional business center.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Hoffman Estates?
sections.html:
The village spans several districts, so the school assigned to a house depends on its address.

  • North of Interstate 90, Township High School District 211 serves high school students.
  • In that northern area, Community Consolidated School District 15 (K to 8) serves addresses east of Huntington Boulevard.
  • Barrington School District 220 (K to 12) serves addresses west of Huntington Boulevard in the same area.
  • Residents west of Barrington Road primarily attend Elgin Area U46.

Most of the village is in Harper College Community College District 512. Libraries that serve residents include the Schaumburg Township District Library, the Barrington Area Library, the Gail Borden Public Library District and the Palatine Township Library. Pace runs bus routes that connect the village to Elgin, Rosemont and other destinations.

Because boundaries run along streets rather than around the village, a seller should check the district for the exact address before putting any school name in a listing.

sections.h2: What does the Village require before a Hoffman Estates sale closes?
sections.html:
The Real Estate Transfer Tax, enacted in 1987, requires the seller to pay a tax whenever real estate is transferred or sold within the village. The tax must be paid and a transfer stamp obtained before closing and recording. The Village prints the cost as $3 per $1,000 of the selling price.

  • Give the Village 48 hours of advance notice. Applications and questions go to transferstamps@vohe.org.
  • Submit the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX-203/EZ Dec) and the deed or other document being recorded.
  • At least five days before buying the stamp, call the Water Department at 847-843-4824 to request a final water bill.
  • Call 847-882-9100 or email the same address to confirm there are no outstanding liens or fines and that the garbage bill is current.
  • Exempt stamps carry a $10.00 administrative fee, need the fully executed deed with the exempt language and signature, and require a final water reading when ownership changes.

Stamps are sold at the Village Hall front counter at 1900 Hassell Road on weekdays during business hours, or by mail with a self-addressed stamped return envelope. Ask the closing attorney or title company who is buying the stamp and when.

sections.h2: How is a Hoffman Estates deed recorded, and what do the state and county charge?
sections.html:
Because the village lies mostly in Cook County, deeds are filed with the Cook County Clerk's recordings division at 118 N. Clark Street. The Clerk's fee page lists $107 for a deed, a total that includes the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a document storage fee, the State Rental Housing Support Fee and a non-government filer fee. Recording by mail with return adds $5 per document.

The Clerk's transfer fee table lists two other charges with the seller as the liable party: .50 per $500.00 for the State of Illinois and .25 per $500.00 for Cook County. The state's statute for this tax is 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

sections.h2: What are the realistic ways to sell a Hoffman Estates house fast?
sections.html:
The route depends on how much time and repair work you can absorb.

  • List on the open market. This reaches the most buyers, but the sale depends on the buyer's financing, an appraisal and an inspection.
  • Sell without an agent. You keep control but take on the paperwork, including the transfer stamp steps above.
  • Accept a cash offer. A cash buyer can often close on a date you pick, and the house sells as it stands, which can help with a tenant-occupied property or a house with deferred repairs.

With any route, work back from the closing date. The 48-hour notice, the five-day water bill request and the lien check all come before the stamp, and the stamp comes before recording. Starting the water bill call early removes the most common delay.

faqs.q: What is the population of Hoffman Estates, IL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 50,858 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 52,530.

faqs.q: How much is the Hoffman Estates transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Village prints the cost as $3 per $1,000 of the selling price, paid by the seller. Exempt stamps have a $10.00 administrative fee.

faqs.q: Which county records deeds for Hoffman Estates?
faqs.a: Cook County, since most of the village lies there. A very small part is in Kane County, so check the parcel's county before sending a deed.

faqs.q: How far ahead must I contact the Village about a transfer stamp?
faqs.a: Give 48 hours of advance notice for processing, and request a final water bill at least five days before buying the stamp by calling 847-843-4824.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Hoffman Estates house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the street. Areas east of Huntington Boulevard in the north are in Community Consolidated School District 15, areas west of it in Barrington District 220, and areas west of Barrington Road mostly in Elgin Area U46.
